title: Retail Store Microservices Deployment on Kubernetes
tagline: End-to-end orchestration of an 8+ service microservices architecture.
description: A production-grade Kubernetes deployment of a polyglot microservices retail platform featuring StatefulSets, MongoDB replication, NGINX ingress routing, and decoupled state management.

details.overview: Flagship project orchestrating 8+ microservices (including React frontend, API gateways, and specialized backend logic) onto a production-ready Kubernetes environment.
details.architecture: React frontend routes through NGINX Ingress to internal services. Stateful services run via StatefulSets backed by persistent storage, while stateless services utilize rolling updates with init containers managing startup dependencies.
features: High-availability MongoDB Replica Set deployment using Kubernetes StatefulSets
Path-based and host-based routing using NGINX Ingress Controller
Init containers used for database migration and service-dependency boot sequencing
Decoupled configuration management with native Kubernetes ConfigMaps and Secrets
folderStructure: k8s/manifests/ – core Deployment, StatefulSet, and Service specs
k8s/ingress/ – NGINX routing and TLS configuration
helm/ – Helm chart for parameterized environment deployment
scripts/ – cluster bootstrap and teardown helpers
lessonsLearned: Proper ordering of service boot cycles via init containers eliminates cascading start failures in microservices
StatefulSet persistent volume claims require explicit reclaim policies to prevent accidental data loss during updates
challenges: Configuring stable MongoDB replica set elections inside a dynamic pod network
Setting precise CPU/Memory requests and limits across 8+ distinct containers to optimize node utilization
futureImprovements: Implement GitOps deployment patterns using ArgoCD
Add automated horizontal pod autoscaling (HPA) based on custom metrics

title: Production CI/CD Pipeline for Kubernetes
tagline: From git push to Kubernetes rollout with security and quality gates built in.
description: An automated CI/CD pipeline built on Jenkins that runs static analysis with SonarQube, security scanning with Trivy, artifact pushing to Nexus/Docker Hub, and zero-downtime deployment to Kubernetes.

details.overview: Automates the software supply chain by integrating code quality enforcement, container image security checks, artifact versioning, and direct Kubernetes deployment.
details.architecture: GitHub Webhook → Jenkins Pipeline → Maven Build & SonarQube Analysis → Trivy CVE Image Scan → Docker Hub / Nexus Push → Rolling deployment to Kubernetes cluster.
features: Hard security gates: pipeline fails immediately if Trivy detects HIGH or CRITICAL CVEs
Quality gate integration enforcing SonarQube rules before artifact creation
Artifact management leveraging Nexus Repository Manager for container and application builds
Zero-downtime rolling updates directly applied to Kubernetes deployments
folderStructure: Jenkinsfile – declarative pipeline definition
k8s/ – deployment and service manifests updated by CI
sonar-project.properties – static analysis thresholds
lessonsLearned: Automated vulnerability scans are only effective if they act as hard pipeline blockers
Caching build dependencies within the agent speeds up containerized builds significantly
challenges: Handling dynamic image tag propagation cleanly from Jenkins down to the Kubernetes manifests
Securing Jenkins credentials for Kubernetes API access without exposing SA tokens
futureImprovements: Migrate to containerized, dynamic Jenkins Kubernetes agents
Incorporate chatops notifications via Slack for pipeline pass/fail status

title: Production Kubernetes Infrastructure with kops on AWS
tagline: Declarative, production-grade Kubernetes cluster management on AWS.
description: Provisioning and managing a custom, highly-available Kubernetes cluster on AWS using kops, managing IAM roles, Route53, and S3 state storage explicitly.

details.overview: Demonstrates production control-plane provisioning without managed cloud shortcuts, handling control plane nodes, worker nodes, state storage, and networking directly.
details.architecture: kops reads cluster specification from an S3 bucket state store, configures Route53 DNS records, provisions EC2 instances across availability zones, and configures RBAC and network overlays.
features: Multi-master control plane setup across AWS Availability Zones
S3 bucket state store for cluster lifecycle and configuration management
Granular AWS IAM policies scoped specifically for node and control-plane permissions
Cluster upgrade and node-pool scaling procedures executed strictly via declarative configs
folderStructure: cluster-manifests/ – kops cluster yaml configurations
iam/ – custom policy definitions for worker node roles
scripts/ – deployment and verification commands
lessonsLearned: Direct cluster management via kops builds a deep understanding of control-plane mechanics compared to managed EKS
DNS resolution via Route53 is critical during initial control-plane API bootstrapping
challenges: Troubleshooting network overlay CNI initialization during cold cluster boots
Fine-tuning IAM permissions for external volume attachments without granting overly permissive admin rights
futureImprovements: Automate kops state updates via GitHub Actions workflows
Integrate cluster autoscaler for worker node pools

title: Persistent Storage Architecture with AWS EBS CSI Driver
tagline: Stateful storage resilience for dynamic cloud workloads.
description: Configuring dynamically provisioned persistent volumes in Kubernetes backed by AWS EBS, ensuring stateful pod storage survives node failures and lifecycle events.

details.overview: Implementation of cloud-native persistent storage using the AWS EBS Container Storage Interface (CSI) driver, enabling dynamic volume provisioning and persistent volume retain/reclaim workflows.
details.architecture: Kubernetes PVC → StorageClass (ebs.csi.aws.com) → AWS EBS CSI Controller → Dynamic EBS Volume creation & attachment to target node via IAM OIDC identity.
features: Dynamic volume provisioning utilizing custom StorageClasses (gp2/gp3)
Configured volume binding modes and expansion capabilities
IAM service account (IRSA) configuration for security-conscious AWS API calls
Demonstrated volume recovery and re-attachment across pod restarts
folderStructure: storage/ – StorageClass, PVC, and PV manifest files
iam/ – OIDC trust policies and IAM role definitions for the CSI driver
test-app/ – sample stateful workload specifications
lessonsLearned: AZ pinning (topology constraints) is essential because EBS volumes are bound to a single availability zone
Dynamic volume expansion requires explicit support inside the StorageClass definition
challenges: Debugging permissions issue between pod service accounts and AWS IAM policies during driver setup
Handling mount-lock timeouts when moving stateful pods across worker nodes
futureImprovements: Implement automated EBS snapshotting routines using VolumeSnapshots
Explore multi-AZ shared storage options using EFS CSI driver

title: Kubernetes Ingress & Network Traffic Management
tagline: Controlling external traffic into the cluster with precision.
description: Advanced HTTP/HTTPS routing configurations using NGINX Ingress Controller on Kubernetes, handling host-based and path-based routing across internal services.

details.overview: A dedicated networking project establishing an entry point for external traffic into a Kubernetes cluster with centralized URL routing, SSL termination, and load balancing.
details.architecture: Incoming web requests → Cloud Load Balancer → NGINX Ingress Controller Pods → Kubernetes Services (ClusterIP) → Target Application Pods.
features: Path-based (/api, /app) and Host-based (app.domain.com) traffic distribution
Centralized SSL/TLS termination at the Ingress layer using Secrets
Custom ingress annotations for request rewriting, rate limiting, and body size limits
Integration with cloud load balancers for external IP allocation
folderStructure: ingress/ – Ingress resource definitions and rewrite rules
services/ – underlying ClusterIP backend applications for routing tests
certs/ – TLS secret templates
lessonsLearned: Host headers must be preserved carefully when rewriting paths at the Ingress proxy layer
Ingress-nginx annotations provide precise control over NGINX location blocks without altering configuration files manually
challenges: Resolving redirect loops when configuring SSL redirect rules alongside external load balancers
Debugging 502 Bad Gateway issues related to container readiness probe timings
futureImprovements: Integrate Cert-Manager for fully automated Let's Encrypt TLS certificate generation
Implement dynamic traffic splitting for blue/green releases via ingress annotations

title: High-Availability MySQL Database Deployment on Kubernetes
tagline: Running mission-critical relational databases reliably on K8s.
description: Deploying a stateful MySQL database cluster featuring primary-replica replication, headless services for network identity, and dynamic volume persistence.

details.overview: A pattern for running stateful SQL workloads in Kubernetes using native primitives to ensure deterministic ordering, stable network identifiers, and automated data replication.
details.architecture: StatefulSet provisions `mysql-0` (Primary/Read-Write) and `mysql-x` (Replicas/Read-Only). A Headless Service provides DNS records for individual pods, and ConfigMaps inject custom MySQL replication configs.
features: StatefulSet management securing stable pod hostnames (`mysql-0`, `mysql-1`) across restarts
Automated initialization scripts via ConfigMaps for replication user creation and binlog tracking
Separation of Read-Write and Read-Only traffic via dedicated Kubernetes Services
Persistent Volume Claims per pod ensuring data isolates correctly
folderStructure: manifests/ – StatefulSet, Headless Service, and ConfigMap definitions
scripts/ – data seed and replication check scripts
lessonsLearned: Headless Services are indispensable for stateful workloads requiring direct pod-to-pod communication
Init containers are vital for cloning database baselines before the MySQL server process boots
challenges: Configuring GTID-based replication reliably during automated pod rollouts
Ensuring clean failover execution without causing split-brain scenarios on storage volumes
futureImprovements: Transition deployment to a managed MySQL Kubernetes Operator (e.g., Presslabs or Percona)
Add automated backup CronJobs targeting AWS S3 storage

title: Dockerized Three-Tier Application Architecture
tagline: Containerizing web, API, and database layers for scalable deployment.
description: Multi-container architecture featuring a Flask backend, MariaDB database, and NGINX web server deployed across isolated Docker networks.

details.overview: A production-styled multi-container setup isolating backend services from web traffic using custom Docker bridge networks and Docker Compose orchestration on AWS EC2.
details.architecture: NGINX handles incoming web requests on port 80/443 and proxies dynamic requests to the Flask API. Flask interacts with MariaDB on an internal non-public Docker network.
features: Decoupled multi-tier isolation using custom Docker bridge networks
Data persistence achieved using Docker named volumes for database storage
NGINX optimized for static asset delivery and API reverse proxying
Single-command boot procedure via Docker Compose
folderStructure: backend/ – Flask app codebase and Dockerfile
nginx/ – NGINX configuration and static files
docker-compose.yml – multi-container orchestration definition
lessonsLearned: Restricting container exposure to specific internal Docker networks drastically reduces attack surface
Multi-stage Docker builds reduce overall image size and cut vulnerability count
challenges: Configuring container start dependency checks to ensure MariaDB was fully initialized before Flask attempted migrations
Managing file permissions across Docker host bind mounts for static assets
futureImprovements: Migrate container specs into Kubernetes manifests
Add dynamic resource capping for CPU and memory usage in Compose
